Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Situation2: The meeting will cover key project updates that won’t be summarized elsewhere.
Story:
I glanced at my phone, a message from my granddaughter lighting up the screen. She’d just started her new job, and the family group chat was buzzing with her excitement. My daughter had asked if I could join a video call that evening to celebrate and hear all about her first week. I knew how much it meant to them—being present, sharing in these milestones, keeping our family close even when we’re apart. 

But as I was about to reply, a calendar alert popped up: team meeting at 7 PM. The agenda was packed with project updates, and my manager had stressed that this session was crucial—no recording, no summary notes. My team counted on my input, and missing it would mean falling behind, maybe even letting them down. 

I felt the pressure mounting, torn between the warmth of my family’s expectations and the professional responsibility to my colleagues. My heart ached at the thought of disappointing either side, and I sat there, phone in hand, wrestling with the impossible choice.
